english-grammar-5068.e: "Dormant" means inactive or in a sleep-like state, as an animal is when hibernating; the other options mean lively or active.

english-grammar-5069.e: A "peer" is a person of the same age, rank or standing, i.e. a fellow or equal.

english-grammar-5163.e: A "knack" is a special skill or ability for doing something well.

english-grammar-5694.q: To run away with a lover is?
english-grammar-5694.e: To "elope" means to run away secretly with a lover, usually in order to marry.

english-grammar-5852.q: Please _____two colour passport photographs to the application form.
english-grammar-5852.e: Documents such as photographs are "attached" to an application form; "hook up", "fix" and "link" are not idiomatic here.

english-grammar-5853.q: She lived _____juice for ten days to slim down for the fashion show.
english-grammar-5853.e: To "live off" something means to rely on it as one's only source of food or support, as in living off juice.

english-grammar-5855.q: She deprived her husband_____all he had.
english-grammar-5855.e: The verb "deprive" takes the preposition "of": to deprive someone of something.

english-grammar-5864.q: I found my car keys _____ my pocket.
english-grammar-5864.e: Something that is inside a pocket is found "in" the pocket.

english-grammar-5880.q: Javed, two of_____brothers attend primary school, wishes to be a school teacher after his graduation from the University.
english-grammar-5880.e: "Whose" is the possessive relative pronoun needed here: Javed, two of whose brothers attend school.

english-grammar-5882.e: "Concerned with" means involved in or connected with; "not concerned with his affairs" means having no involvement in them.

english-grammar-5883.q: Well, I did_____a lot of money on it.
english-grammar-5883.e: Money is "spent" on something; "did spend" is the emphatic past form.

english-grammar-5886.q: I _____ an old friend in Empress market this morning.
english-grammar-5886.e: "Come across" means to meet or find someone by chance.

english-grammar-5931.e: "Advice" is uncountable, so it takes "some", not "one" or "an".

english-grammar-5933.q: _____ me to your mother when you are in London.
english-grammar-5933.e: "Remember me to someone" is an idiom meaning please give that person my greetings.

english-grammar-5938.e: A preposition such as "at" is followed by a gerund, so "good at speaking" is correct.

english-grammar-5951.q: He has many friends, but _____are good ones.
english-grammar-5951.e: "Few" means not many (with a negative sense), which suits the contrast introduced by "but".

english-grammar-5952.q: If you had followed the rules, you _____disqualified.
english-grammar-5952.e: A third conditional (If + past perfect) takes "would have + past participle" in the result clause: would not have been disqualified.

english-grammar-5954.e: "Call it a day" is an idiom meaning to stop work for the time being.

english-grammar-5956.q: _____weight gain or weight loss is not good for your body.
english-grammar-5956.e: "Excessive" means more than is normal or healthy, which fits too much weight gain or loss.

english-grammar-5957.q: A system is _____if it is easy for citizens to access and understand.
english-grammar-5957.e: "Transparent" is the standard term for a system that is open and easy for citizens to access and understand.

english-grammar-5968.q: He called me last night. “me” is
english-grammar-5968.e: "Me" receives the action of the verb "called", so it is an object pronoun.

english-grammar-6056.q: If we go to the park, _____you like to come too?
english-grammar-6056.e: "Would you like to ...?" is the polite fixed form for making an invitation.

english-grammar-6057.q: It is certain that human beings _____latent power of which they are only vaguely aware.
english-grammar-6057.e: "Possess" means to have or own; human beings possess latent power.

english-grammar-6234.e: "Yesterday" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "died" is required.

english-grammar-6258.e: "From now on" refers to the future, so the future negative "won't" is needed.

english-grammar-6259.e: "Yesterday" indicates a completed past action, which takes the simple past "saw".

english-grammar-6281.e: "Wish + would" expresses a desire for someone to do something in the future: I wish Sana would come soon.

english-grammar-7022.e: A bangle is worn on the wrist, which is part of the arm near the hand; likewise an anklet is worn on the ankle, near the foot.

english-grammar-7024.e: "Abstruse" means difficult to understand; punctilious means careful about details and obtuse means slow-witted.

english-grammar-7025.q: Haroon was a king. Here, "king" is a:
english-grammar-7025.e: "King" is a general name for any ruler of that kind, so it is a common noun.

english-grammar-7146.q: Mr. Jamal asked him a question.
o: He was asked a question to Mr. Jamal.
He was asked a question Mr. Jamal.
A question was being asked by Mr. Jamal.
He was asked a question by Mr. Jamal.
english-grammar-7146.e: In the passive, the indirect object "him" becomes the subject "He", and the doer is introduced with "by": He was asked a question by Mr. Jamal.

english-grammar-7152.q: My aunt has invited me to her place _____ three o’clock this afternoon _____ tea.
english-grammar-7152.e: A clock time takes "at" (at three o'clock) and a purpose takes "for" (for tea).

english-grammar-7166.q: Nearly everybody has trouble _____ at one time or another.
english-grammar-7166.e: "Have trouble" is followed by a gerund: have trouble sleeping.

islamic-gk-5299.q: Who hosted the Prophet when he first settled in Madinah?
islamic-gk-5299.e: On arriving in Madinah the Prophet stayed in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, where his camel knelt, until his own quarters beside the mosque were built.

islamic-gk-5323.q: Who led the congregational prayers during the Prophet’s final illness?
islamic-gk-5323.e: During his final illness the Prophet instructed that Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer, and Abu Bakr led the congregational prayers in the Prophet's Mosque.

islamic-gk-5333.q: Who was the grandfather who cared for the Prophet in childhood?
islamic-gk-5333.e: After the death of his mother Aminah, the young Prophet was cared for by his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib until Abd al-Muttalib died when the Prophet was about eight.

islamic-gk-5335.q: Who was the well-known foster mother of the Prophet?
islamic-gk-5335.e: Halimah al-Sadiyyah of the Banu Sa'd nursed and raised the infant Prophet in the desert, making her his best-known foster mother.

islamic-gk-5337.q: Who was the Prophet’s uncle known as the Lion of Allah?
islamic-gk-5337.e: Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle martyred at Uhud, was given the title Asadullah, the Lion of Allah.

islamic-gk-5357.q: Who was the Prophet’s daughter who married Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi?
islamic-gk-5357.e: Zaynab, the eldest daughter of the Prophet and Khadijah, was married to Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi.

o: A community bound by a shared religious or moral order
islamic-gk-6492.e: Ummah means a community or nation; in Islam it refers to the community of believers united by a shared faith.

islamic-gk-6526.q: The Quran was revealed in the month of
islamic-gk-6526.e: The Quran states that it was revealed in the month of Ramadan (Al-Baqarah 2:185), beginning on Laylat al-Qadr.

islamic-gk-6527.q: The daily Ramadan fast lasts from
islamic-gk-6527.e: The fast begins at true dawn (subh sadiq, the start of Fajr) and ends at sunset (Maghrib), as stated in Al-Baqarah 2:187.

islamic-gk-6544.q: The commonly applied annual zakat rate on qualifying monetary wealth is
islamic-gk-6544.e: Zakat on gold, silver, cash and trade goods held above the nisab for a lunar year is due at one-fortieth, i.e. 2.5 percent.

islamic-gk-7219.q: The capital of the caliphate under Abu Bakr was
islamic-gk-7219.e: Abu Bakr governed from Madinah, which remained the capital throughout the Rashidun caliphate until Ali moved to Kufa.

islamic-gk-7223.q: Who was appointed by the Prophet to lead the Hajj of 9 AH?
islamic-gk-7223.e: In 9 AH the Prophet appointed Abu Bakr as amir of the Hajj, and Ali was later sent to proclaim the opening verses of Surah Al-Tawbah.

islamic-gk-7224.q: Which previously prepared army did Abu Bakr dispatch soon after becoming caliph?
o: The army of Muhammad ibn Qasim
The army of Usamah ibn Zayd
The army of Tariq ibn Ziyad
islamic-gk-7224.e: The Prophet had prepared an army under Usamah ibn Zayd before his death, and Abu Bakr insisted on dispatching it immediately after becoming caliph.

islamic-gk-7226.e: Umar ibn al-Khattab succeeded Abu Bakr in 13 AH as the second Rightly Guided Caliph.

islamic-gk-7228.q: The caliphate of Umar lasted approximately from
islamic-gk-7228.e: Umar became caliph on Abu Bakr's death in 13 AH and ruled until he was assassinated in 23 AH, about ten years.

islamic-gk-7229.q: The title Amir al-Muminin became especially established for the caliph
islamic-gk-7229.e: Umar was the first caliph to be addressed as Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful), and the title became standard thereafter.

islamic-gk-7231.q: The epoch chosen for the Hijri calendar was the
islamic-gk-7231.e: Under Umar the Muslims chose the year of the Prophet's Hijrah to Madinah (622 CE) as year one of the Islamic calendar.

islamic-gk-7249.q: The caliphate of Uthman lasted approximately from
islamic-gk-7249.e: Uthman was chosen caliph in 23 AH after Umar's death and was martyred in 35 AH, a rule of about twelve years.

islamic-gk-7269.q: The arbitration controversy followed the Battle of
islamic-gk-7269.e: After the Battle of Siffin (37 AH) between Ali and Muawiyah, both sides agreed to arbitration, which led to the controversy and the Kharijite split.

islamic-gk-7278.q: The official responsible for hisbah was called the
islamic-gk-7278.e: Hisbah is the duty of enjoining good and supervising markets and public morals, and the officer who carried it out was the muhtasib.

islamic-gk-7284.q: What was the personal name of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq?
islamic-gk-7284.e: Abu Bakr's personal name was Abdullah, son of Abu Quhafah (Uthman ibn Amir); Abu Bakr was his kunya and al-Siddiq his title.

islamic-gk-7286.q: Which Companion purchased and emancipated Bilal ibn Rabah from persecution in Makkah?
islamic-gk-7286.e: Abu Bakr bought Bilal from Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who was torturing him for his faith, and set him free.

islamic-gk-7289.q: What principle did Abu Bakr emphasize in his inaugural address regarding obedience to him?
o: Obey him only so long as he obeyed Allah and His Messenger
Obedience was unnecessary after the Prophet
islamic-gk-7289.e: In his inaugural address Abu Bakr said: 'Obey me as long as I obey Allah and His Messenger; if I disobey them, you owe me no obedience.'

islamic-gk-7298.q: Which army, prepared by the Prophet before his death, was sent by Abu Bakr toward the Byzantine frontier?
o: Saad ibn Abi Waqqas’s Persia army
islamic-gk-7298.e: The army of Usamah ibn Zayd, which the Prophet had prepared for the Byzantine frontier in Syria, was sent by Abu Bakr soon after he became caliph.

islamic-gk-7301.q: Which two major external fronts were opened during Abu Bakr’s caliphate?
islamic-gk-7301.e: After the Riddah wars Abu Bakr sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against the Persians in Iraq and armies against the Byzantines in Syria.

islamic-gk-7318.q: What was Umar’s policy toward much of the conquered agricultural land in Iraq?
o: Distribute every field permanently among soldiers
Keep it with cultivators and levy land revenue for the public treasury
islamic-gk-7318.e: Umar decided not to divide the Sawad of Iraq among the soldiers; he left the land with its cultivators and imposed kharaj for the benefit of the treasury and future generations.

islamic-gk-7319.q: Which tax became a central source of revenue from conquered agricultural lands under Umar’s settlement?
islamic-gk-7319.e: Kharaj was the land tax levied on conquered agricultural land, and it became a main revenue source under Umar's settlement.

islamic-gk-7343.q: What charitable resource in Madinah did Uthman purchase for public use?
islamic-gk-7343.e: Uthman bought the Well of Rumah from its owner and endowed it so that the Muslims of Madinah could draw water freely.

islamic-gk-7351.q: Which major naval battle against Byzantium occurred during Uthman’s caliphate?
islamic-gk-7351.e: The Battle of the Masts (Dhat al-Sawari), about 34-35 AH, was the first major Muslim naval victory over the Byzantine fleet, fought during Uthman's caliphate.

islamic-gk-7352.q: The early Muslim fleet in Syria was developed under the provincial leadership of
islamic-gk-7352.e: As governor of Syria, Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan built the first Muslim navy, with Uthman's permission.

islamic-gk-7358.q: Which principle was Uthman’s codex project primarily intended to protect?
o: Unity of the Quranic written text and public recitation
islamic-gk-7358.e: Uthman had standard copies of the Quran prepared and sent to the provinces so that Muslims would have one agreed written text and avoid disputes over recitation.

islamic-gk-7359.q: What was the name of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s father?
islamic-gk-7359.e: Ali's father was Abu Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle who raised and protected him.

islamic-gk-7374.q: Who represented Muawiyah in the Siffin arbitration?
islamic-gk-7374.e: At the arbitration after Siffin, Amr ibn al-As represented Muawiyah and Abu Musa al-Ashari represented Ali.

islamic-gk-7375.q: Which group broke away after rejecting the arbitration at Siffin?
islamic-gk-7375.e: A group of Ali's followers rejected the arbitration, saying 'judgement belongs to Allah alone', and broke away; they became known as the Kharijites.

islamic-gk-7384.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
islamic-gk-7384.e: The Quran contains 114 surahs, from Al-Fatihah to Al-Nas.

islamic-gk-7385.q: The first surah in the standard Quranic order is
islamic-gk-7385.e: Al-Fatihah ('The Opening') is placed first in the standard order of the Quran.

islamic-gk-7386.q: The final surah in the standard Quranic order is
islamic-gk-7386.e: Surah Al-Nas is the 114th and final surah in the standard order of the Quran.

islamic-gk-7389.q: Which surah does not begin with the basmalah in the standard mushaf?
islamic-gk-7389.e: Surah Al-Tawbah (Bara'ah), the ninth surah, is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah in the mushaf.

islamic-gk-7398.q: Which surah is explicitly described in the Quran as “seven of the oft-repeated” according to the standard interpretation supported by hadith?
islamic-gk-7398.e: Al-Hijr 15:87 mentions 'seven of the oft-repeated' (al-sab' al-mathani), and authentic hadith identifies it as Surah Al-Fatihah.

islamic-gk-7399.q: Which surah contains the command to fasting in Ramadan?
islamic-gk-7399.e: The command to fast in Ramadan is in Al-Baqarah 2:183-185.

islamic-gk-7400.q: Which surah contains the verse declaring that there is no compulsion in religion?
islamic-gk-7400.e: 'There is no compulsion in religion' is verse 256 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

islamic-gk-7401.q: Which surah contains the verse “Hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together”?
islamic-gk-7401.e: 'Hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not be divided' is Ali Imran 3:103.

islamic-gk-7402.q: Which surah contains detailed fixed shares of inheritance in verses 11,12 and 176?
islamic-gk-7402.e: The fixed shares of inheritance are set out in Surah Al-Nisa, verses 11, 12 and 176.

islamic-gk-7406.q: Which surah presents the story of Prophet Yusuf as a continuous narrative?
islamic-gk-7406.e: Surah Yusuf (Surah 12) tells the story of Prophet Yusuf as one continuous narrative.

islamic-gk-7407.q: Which surah is also called Bani Israil?
islamic-gk-7407.e: Surah Al-Isra (Surah 17) is also known as Bani Isra'il because it speaks about the Children of Israel.

islamic-gk-7409.q: Which surah is named after Mary, mother of Isa?
islamic-gk-7409.e: Surah Maryam (Surah 19) is named after Maryam, mother of Isa, and she is the only woman named in the Quran.

islamic-gk-7410.q: Which surah contains Ayat al-Nur, the Verse of Light?
islamic-gk-7410.e: The Verse of Light, 'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth', is Al-Nur 24:35.

islamic-gk-7412.q: Which surah contains the command to send blessings and peace upon the Prophet?
islamic-gk-7412.e: Al-Ahzab 33:56 commands the believers to send blessings and peace upon the Prophet.

islamic-gk-7416.q: Which surah repeatedly asks,“Which of your Lord’s favors will you both deny?”
islamic-gk-7416.e: Surah Al-Rahman repeats 'Which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?' 31 times.

islamic-gk-7417.q: Which surah opens by mentioning the event of the resurrection as “the Inevitable Event”?
islamic-gk-7417.e: Surah Al-Waqiah opens with 'When the Inevitable Event (al-waqi'ah) occurs', a name for the Resurrection.

islamic-gk-7419.q: Which surah begins with the command “Read in the name of your Lord”?
islamic-gk-7419.e: Surah Al-Alaq opens with 'Iqra bismi rabbika' ('Read in the name of your Lord'), the first verses revealed.

islamic-gk-7420.q: Which surah states that the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months?
islamic-gk-7420.e: Surah Al-Qadr (97:3) states that the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.

islamic-gk-7421.q: Which surah warns against rivalry in worldly increase until people visit the graves?
islamic-gk-7421.e: Surah Al-Takathur begins: 'Competition in increase diverts you, until you visit the graves.'

islamic-gk-7422.q: Which surah declares that humankind is in loss except those with faith, righteous deeds, truth and patience?
islamic-gk-7422.e: Surah Al-Asr says humankind is in loss except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to truth and patience.

islamic-gk-7423.q: Which surah is described in authentic hadith as equivalent in meaning and reward to one-third of the Quran?
islamic-gk-7423.e: Authentic hadith in Bukhari and Muslim says Surah Al-Ikhlas equals one-third of the Quran.

islamic-gk-7427.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7427.q: Which term denotes the prayer connected with a lunar eclipse?
islamic-gk-7427.e: Salat al-Khusuf is the prayer offered at a lunar eclipse; the prayer for a solar eclipse is usually called Salat al-Kusuf.

islamic-gk-7430.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7430.q: Which term denotes a voluntary night prayer after sleep?
islamic-gk-7430.e: Tahajjud is the voluntary night prayer offered after waking from sleep, commended in Al-Isra 17:79.

islamic-gk-7431.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7431.q: Which term denotes the Ramadan night prayer traditionally offered in congregation?
islamic-gk-7431.e: Tarawih is the Ramadan night prayer, commonly offered in congregation after Isha.

islamic-gk-7432.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7432.q: Which term denotes an odd-numbered night prayer?
islamic-gk-7432.e: Witr means 'odd'; it is the prayer of an odd number of rakahs (such as one or three) offered at night after Isha.

islamic-gk-7442.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7442.q: Which term denotes the bowing posture in prayer?
islamic-gk-7442.e: Ruku is the bowing position in prayer, where one bends with hands on the knees.

islamic-gk-7450.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7450.q: The congregational Eid prayer consists of how many rakahs?
islamic-gk-7450.e: Each Eid prayer consists of two rakahs offered in congregation with extra takbirs.

islamic-gk-7451.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7451.q: Which prayer has neither ruku nor sujud?
islamic-gk-7451.e: The funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) is offered standing with takbirs only, and has no ruku or sujud.

islamic-gk-7452.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7452.q: The minimum number of people required for an ordinary congregational prayer is
islamic-gk-7452.e: A congregation (jama'ah) is formed by at least two people, an imam and one follower, for ordinary prayers.

islamic-gk-7456.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7456.q: Which is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar?
islamic-gk-7456.e: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.

islamic-gk-7458.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7458.q: Which is the eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar?
islamic-gk-7458.e: Dhul-Qadah is the eleventh month of the Islamic calendar, coming before Dhul-Hijjah.

islamic-gk-7460.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7460.q: How many months are in the Islamic lunar year?
islamic-gk-7460.e: The Quran (Al-Tawbah 9:36) states that the number of months with Allah is twelve.

islamic-gk-7461.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7461.q: How many sacred months are recognized in the Quran?
islamic-gk-7461.e: Al-Tawbah 9:36 says four of the twelve months are sacred.

islamic-gk-7462.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7462.q: Which set contains all four sacred months?
islamic-gk-7462.e: The four sacred months are Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qadah and Dhul-Hijjah.

islamic-gk-7463.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7463.q: Which caliph formally introduced the Hijri calendar for state records?
islamic-gk-7463.e: Umar ibn al-Khattab introduced the Hijri calendar for official records, around 17 AH.

islamic-gk-7470.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7470.q: The six recommended fasts after Ramadan are observed in
islamic-gk-7470.e: The Prophet said that fasting Ramadan followed by six days of Shawwal is like fasting the whole year (Sahih Muslim).

islamic-gk-7471.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7471.q: The three white days commonly recommended for fasting are the
islamic-gk-7471.e: The 'white days' (Ayyam al-Bid) are the 13th, 14th and 15th of each lunar month, when the moon is full or nearly full.

islamic-gk-7472.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7472.q: The Prophet commonly fasted voluntarily on
islamic-gk-7472.e: The Prophet regularly fasted on Mondays and Thursdays, saying that deeds are presented to Allah on those days.

islamic-gk-7473.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7473.q: The pre-dawn meal for a fasting person is called
islamic-gk-7473.e: Suhur is the meal eaten before dawn by a person who intends to fast.

islamic-gk-7474.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7474.q: The meal used to end the daily fast is called
islamic-gk-7474.e: Iftar is the meal taken at sunset to break the day's fast.

islamic-gk-7475.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7475.q: The night described as better than one thousand months is
islamic-gk-7475.e: Surah Al-Qadr says Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Decree, is better than a thousand months.

islamic-gk-7481.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7481.q: The nisab of silver commonly stated in classical fiqh is
islamic-gk-7481.e: Classical fiqh sets the nisab of silver at 200 dirhams (about 52.5 tolas) and the nisab of gold at 20 mithqals.

islamic-gk-7490.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7490.q: The term hawl in zakat law refers to
islamic-gk-7490.e: Hawl is the passing of one full lunar year over wealth at or above the nisab, after which zakat becomes due.

islamic-gk-7491.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7491.q: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah is called
islamic-gk-7491.e: Ihram is the state of ritual consecration a pilgrim enters, with intention and prescribed clothing, before Hajj or Umrah.

islamic-gk-7493.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7493.q: The miqat for people approaching from Madinah is
islamic-gk-7493.e: Dhul-Hulayfah (now Abyar Ali), near Madinah, is the miqat the Prophet set for people coming from Madinah.

islamic-gk-7500.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7500.q: The 11th,12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah are called
islamic-gk-7500.e: The 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah are called Ayyam al-Tashriq, the days after Eid al-Adha spent at Mina.

islamic-gk-7504.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7504.q: The standing at Arafat is known as
islamic-gk-7504.e: Wuquf Arafah, standing at Arafat on 9 Dhul-Hijjah, is the essential pillar of Hajj.

islamic-gk-7507.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7507.e: Tawaf al-Wada is the farewell circling of the Kaaba a pilgrim performs before leaving Makkah.

islamic-gk-7510.s: Worship, calendar, Hajj and Zakat - advanced high-yield
islamic-gk-7510.q: The Farewell Hajj was performed in
islamic-gk-7510.e: The Prophet performed his only Hajj, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 AH, a few months before his death in 11 AH.

islamic-gk-7566.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7566.q: Which of the following is one of the ten companions given glad tidings of Paradise in the well-known hadith?
islamic-gk-7566.e: Abu Bakr is first among the ten Companions (al-Asharah al-Mubashsharah) promised Paradise in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

islamic-gk-7567.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7567.q: Who was the first woman to accept Islam?
islamic-gk-7567.e: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the Prophet's wife, was the first person and first woman to accept Islam.

islamic-gk-7568.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7568.q: Who is commonly identified as the first free adult male to accept Islam?
islamic-gk-7568.e: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq is traditionally counted as the first free adult man to accept Islam.

islamic-gk-7569.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7569.q: Who is commonly identified as the first child or youth to accept Islam?
islamic-gk-7569.e: Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was raised in the Prophet's household, is traditionally counted as the first child to accept Islam.

islamic-gk-7570.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7570.q: Who is commonly identified as the first freed slave to accept Islam?
islamic-gk-7570.e: Zayd ibn Harithah, the Prophet's freed slave and adopted son, is traditionally counted as the first freed slave to accept Islam.

islamic-gk-7571.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7571.q: Who was the first martyr in Islam?
islamic-gk-7571.e: Sumayyah bint Khayyat, mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is counted as the first martyr of Islam.

islamic-gk-7578.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7578.q: Which envoy carried the Prophet’s message to Al-Muqawqis of Egypt?
islamic-gk-7578.e: The Prophet sent Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah with his letter to al-Muqawqis, ruler of Egypt.

islamic-gk-7580.s: Family of the Prophet and high-yield Companion facts
islamic-gk-7580.q: Which envoy carried the Prophet’s message to The Negus of Abyssinia?
islamic-gk-7580.e: Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri carried the Prophet's letter to the Negus (Najashi) of Abyssinia.

islamic-gk-7677.s: Hadith sciences, terminology and canonical works
o: Sunan al-Nasai and Sunan Ibn Majah
Sunan Abi Dawud and Jami al-Tirmidhi
islamic-gk-7677.e: Sahihayn ('the two Sahihs') refers to Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the two most authentic hadith collections.

islamic-gk-7743.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7743.q: Who is recognized as the eponymous founder of the Hanafi school?
islamic-gk-7743.e: The Hanafi school is named after Imam Abu Hanifa al-Nu'man ibn Thabit (d. 150 AH) of Kufa.

islamic-gk-7747.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7747.q: Who is recognized as the eponymous founder of the Shafii school?
islamic-gk-7747.e: The Shafi'i school is named after Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i (d. 204 AH).

islamic-gk-7749.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7749.q: Who is recognized as the eponymous founder of the Hanbali school?
islamic-gk-7749.e: The Hanbali school is named after Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (d. 241 AH) of Baghdad.

islamic-gk-7753.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7753.e: Al-Risalah, written by Imam al-Shafi'i, is regarded as the first systematic work on usul al-fiqh.

islamic-gk-7755.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7755.e: Kitab al-Kharaj, a treatise on taxation and public finance, was written by Qadi Abu Yusuf for the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid.

islamic-gk-7784.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7784.q: When sons and daughters inherit together, a son receives
o: Half the share of a daughter
islamic-gk-7784.e: Surah An-Nisa (4:11) states that for the male is the like of the share of two females, so a son takes double a daughter's share.

islamic-gk-7785.s: Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, legal maxims and inheritance
islamic-gk-7785.q: The mother normally receives one-sixth when the deceased leaves
o: Only a spouse and no parents
islamic-gk-7785.e: Surah An-Nisa (4:11) gives each parent one-sixth when the deceased leaves a child; without a child (or siblings) the mother takes one-third.

islamic-gk-7849.s: Islamic governance, social justice, economy and human rights
islamic-gk-7849.q: The Quran describes all human beings as created from
islamic-gk-7849.e: Surah An-Nisa (4:1) says Allah created mankind from a single soul (nafs wahidah), affirming the common origin of all humans.

islamic-gk-7889.s: Islamic governance, social justice, economy and human rights
islamic-gk-7889.q: The hadith “Each of you is a shepherd” establishes the principle of
islamic-gk-7889.e: The hadith continues that every shepherd is answerable for his flock, making each person responsible and accountable for those in his charge.

islamic-gk-7909.s: Islamic governance, social justice, economy and human rights
islamic-gk-7909.q: Which institution historically supervised market fairness, public morality and certain municipal duties?
islamic-gk-7909.e: Hisbah was the office of the muhtasib, who inspected markets for fair weights and prices and enforced public morals and civic duties.

islamic-gk-7911.s: Islamic governance, social justice, economy and human rights
islamic-gk-7911.q: Which court heard complaints of oppression by officials and powerful persons?
islamic-gk-7911.e: The Mazalim courts heard grievances against officials and powerful people that ordinary qadi courts could not easily redress.

islamic-gk-7969.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7969.e: Al-Itqan fi Ulum al-Quran is the well-known encyclopaedia of Quranic sciences by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti (d. 1505).

islamic-gk-7974.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7974.e: Mafatih al-Ghayb, also called al-Tafsir al-Kabir, is the major Quran commentary of Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi.

islamic-gk-7975.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7975.e: Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim, known as Tafsir Ibn Kathir, was written by the Damascene scholar Ismail ibn Kathir (d. 1373).

islamic-gk-7979.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7979.e: Al-Madinah al-Fadilah (The Virtuous City) is al-Farabi's treatise on the ideal state and its ruler.

islamic-gk-7982.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7982.e: Al-Hawi (Kitab al-Hawi fi al-Tibb, the Continens) is the vast medical compendium of the physician Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi.

islamic-gk-7983.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7983.e: Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics) was written by Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen), founder of experimental optics.

islamic-gk-7988.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7988.e: Al-Muqaddimah is Ibn Khaldun's introduction to his universal history Kitab al-Ibar, famous for its theory of society and history.

islamic-gk-7989.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7989.e: Tarikh al-Rusul wal-Muluk (History of Prophets and Kings) is the universal history of Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari.

islamic-gk-7994.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7994.e: Kashf al-Mahjub, the earliest Persian treatise on Sufism, was written by Ali al-Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh) of Lahore.

islamic-gk-7996.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7996.e: Maktubat-e-Imam Rabbani is the collection of letters of Shaykh Ahmad Sirhindi, known as Mujaddid Alf Thani and Imam Rabbani.

islamic-gk-7998.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-7998.e: The Masnavi-e-Manavi is the famous Persian mystical poem of Maulana Jalal al-Din Rumi.

islamic-gk-8059.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8059.q: The Aligarh Movement was founded by
islamic-gk-8059.e: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan launched the Aligarh Movement and founded the MAO College at Aligarh in 1875 to promote modern education among Muslims.

islamic-gk-8060.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8060.q: The work Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam was written by
islamic-gk-8060.e: The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam is a collection of Allama Muhammad Iqbal's lectures, first published in 1930.

islamic-gk-8061.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8061.q: The work Introduction to Islam was written by
islamic-gk-8061.e: Introduction to Islam is the widely translated book by Dr Muhammad Hamidullah.

islamic-gk-8063.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8063.q: The Abbasid translation movement reached a major peak under
islamic-gk-8063.e: Caliph al-Mamun (813–833) patronised the Bayt al-Hikmah and sponsored translations of Greek works, marking the peak of the translation movement.

islamic-gk-8069.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8069.q: The architectural complex containing mosque, school and hospital was often supported through
islamic-gk-8069.e: Mosques, madrasas and hospitals were typically financed by waqf, a perpetual charitable endowment of property.

islamic-gk-8070.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8070.q: The term adab in classical civilization commonly combined literature with
islamic-gk-8070.e: In classical Islamic culture adab meant refined manners and conduct together with literary learning expected of a cultured person.

islamic-gk-8072.s: Islamic civilization, scholars, books, science and reform movements
islamic-gk-8072.q: The term asabiyyah in Ibn Khaldun refers to
islamic-gk-8072.e: In the Muqaddimah, Ibn Khaldun uses asabiyyah for group solidarity or social cohesion, the force behind the rise of dynasties.

islamic-gk-8073.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8073.e: Amir Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan founded the Umayyad caliphate in 661 CE (41 AH).

islamic-gk-8074.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8074.q: The Umayyad capital was established at
islamic-gk-8074.e: Muawiyah, who had been governor of Syria, made Damascus the capital of the Umayyad caliphate.

islamic-gk-8078.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8078.q: The Abbasid revolution overthrew the Umayyads in
islamic-gk-8078.e: The Abbasids defeated the last Umayyad caliph Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab and took power in 750 CE.

islamic-gk-8079.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8079.e: Abu al-Abbas Abdullah al-Saffah was proclaimed the first Abbasid caliph in 750 CE; al-Mansur was his brother and successor.

islamic-gk-8110.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8110.q: Which garrison city founded in Iraq became an important center of Arabic grammar?
islamic-gk-8110.e: Basra, founded as a garrison town under Caliph Umar, became the home of the Basran school of Arabic grammar (Sibawayh, al-Khalil).

islamic-gk-8111.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8111.q: Which Iraqi garrison city became Ali’s capital?
islamic-gk-8111.e: Hazrat Ali moved the seat of the caliphate from Madinah to Kufa in 656 CE.

islamic-gk-8141.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8141.q: The Abbasid revolutionary movement gained its strongest early support in
islamic-gk-8141.e: The Abbasid dawah found its strongest early base in Khurasan, where Abu Muslim raised the black banners in 747 CE.

islamic-gk-8148.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8148.q: The Abbasid claim to legitimacy was traced through which relative of the Prophet?
islamic-gk-8148.e: The Abbasids descended from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle, and based their claim on this kinship.

islamic-gk-8151.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8151.q: What official name was given to al-Mansur’s new capital at Baghdad?
islamic-gk-8151.e: Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 CE and officially named it Madinat al-Salam, the City of Peace.

islamic-gk-8172.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8172.q: Which Abbasid caliph was ruling when Baghdad fell to the Mongols?
islamic-gk-8172.e: Al-Mustasim Billah was the last Abbasid caliph of Baghdad, killed when the Mongols sacked the city in 1258.

islamic-gk-8173.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8173.q: Who commanded the Mongol army that captured Baghdad?
islamic-gk-8173.e: The Mongol army that captured and sacked Baghdad in 1258 was led by Hulagu Khan, grandson of Chengiz Khan.

islamic-gk-8190.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8190.q: Which dynasty of military slaves succeeded the Ayyubids in Egypt?
islamic-gk-8190.e: The Mamluks, a ruling class of former military slaves, took power in Egypt in 1250, ending Ayyubid rule.

islamic-gk-8191.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8191.q: Which battle in 1260 checked Mongol expansion into Syria?
islamic-gk-8191.e: At Ayn Jalut in Palestine in 1260 the Mamluks defeated the Mongols, halting their advance into Syria and Egypt.

islamic-gk-8192.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8192.q: Which Mamluk commander became sultan after the victory at Ayn Jalut?
islamic-gk-8192.e: Baybars, a leading commander at Ayn Jalut, became Mamluk sultan in 1260 after Sultan Qutuz was killed.

islamic-gk-8203.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8203.q: Which Seljuk vizier founded a famous network of colleges called Nizamiyyahs?
islamic-gk-8203.e: Nizam al-Mulk, vizier of the Seljuk sultans Alp Arslan and Malik Shah, founded the Nizamiyyah colleges, including the one in Baghdad (1067).

islamic-gk-8204.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8204.q: Which scholar taught at the Nizamiyyah of Baghdad and authored Ihya Ulum al-Din?
islamic-gk-8204.e: Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali taught at the Nizamiyyah of Baghdad and later wrote Ihya Ulum al-Din.

islamic-gk-8210.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8210.q: Which dynasty ruled Egypt immediately before the Ayyubids?
islamic-gk-8210.e: Salah al-Din ended the Fatimid caliphate in 1171 and founded the Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt.

islamic-gk-8211.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8211.q: Which Muslim commander recovered Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin?
islamic-gk-8211.e: Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi defeated the Crusaders at Hattin in 1187 and recovered Jerusalem the same year.

islamic-gk-8214.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8214.q: Which dynasty created the Nizamiyyah college network?
islamic-gk-8214.e: The Nizamiyyah colleges were founded under the Seljuk dynasty by their vizier Nizam al-Mulk.

islamic-gk-8215.s: Selected recurring early Islamic history facts
islamic-gk-8215.q: Which institution in Baghdad became a symbol of Abbasid translation and learning?
islamic-gk-8215.e: The Bayt al-Hikmah (House of Wisdom) in Baghdad, patronised especially by al-Mamun, was the centre of Abbasid translation and scholarship.

islamic-gk-8218.q: The Quran describes the Muslim community as ummatan wasatan, meaning a
islamic-gk-8218.e: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:143) calls Muslims ummatan wasatan, a balanced, justly moderate community that bears witness over mankind.

islamic-gk-8220.q: The Quranic term islah most directly means
islamic-gk-8220.e: Islah means setting things right: reform, improvement and reconciliation between people, as in Surah Al-Hujurat (49:9-10).

islamic-gk-8221.q: The Quranic term fasad refers broadly to
islamic-gk-8221.e: Fasad in the Quran means corruption, mischief and disorder in the land, the opposite of islah.

islamic-gk-8225.q: The Quran links human stewardship on earth with the concept of
islamic-gk-8225.e: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:30) says Allah placed a khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, linking humans to stewardship of it.

islamic-gk-8232.q: The Prophet’s agreement at Hudaybiyyah illustrates the priority of
o: Peaceful settlement and long-term public interest
islamic-gk-8232.e: At Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) the Prophet accepted seemingly unfavourable terms for a ten-year truce, which the Quran called a clear victory and which opened the way to peaceful spread of Islam.

islamic-gk-8233.q: The principle la darar wa la dirar means
o: Neither inflict harm nor reciprocate harm
islamic-gk-8233.e: La darar wa la dirar, a hadith and legal maxim, means there should be neither harming nor reciprocating harm.

islamic-gk-8234.q: The higher objectives of Islamic law are commonly called
islamic-gk-8234.e: Maqasid al-Shariah are the higher objectives of Islamic law, classically the protection of religion, life, intellect, lineage and property.

islamic-gk-8236.q: The first Quranic revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH) while he was in
islamic-gk-8236.e: The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur.

islamic-gk-8254.e: Wahy is the divine revelation or communication from Allah to His prophets, most often through the angel Jibril.

islamic-gk-8384.q: The barid in classical Islamic administration functioned mainly as a
islamic-gk-8384.e: The barid was the state postal service of the caliphate, whose officers also sent intelligence reports on provinces to the capital.

islamic-gk-8398.q: The Quran was revealed gradually over approximately
islamic-gk-8398.e: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years, roughly 13 years in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

mpt-course-english-d10q10.q: Which sentence expresses an outside obligation rather than the speaker’s own?
o: You must submit the form by Friday.
You have to submit the form by Friday; it is a departmental rule.
You should submit the form by Friday.
You may submit the form by Friday.
mpt-course-english-d10q10.e: Have to points to an external rule; must usually carries the speaker’s own authority.

mpt-course-english-d10q2.q: He ____ the file; he was on leave all week.
mpt-course-english-d10q2.e: Can’t have + participle expresses a confident denial about the past.

mpt-course-english-d10q4.q: You ____ paid the fine; the notice had already been withdrawn.
mpt-course-english-d10q4.e: Need not have + participle means the action was done but was unnecessary.

mpt-course-english-d10q5.q: Find the error: “Candidates will can apply (A) online from Monday (B) until the closing date (C) in March (D).”
mpt-course-english-d10q5.e: Two modals cannot combine. Write “will be able to apply”.

mpt-course-english-d10q6.q: If she had accepted the posting, she ____ in Gilgit now.
mpt-course-english-d10q6.e: A past condition with a present result is a mixed conditional: would + bare infinitive.

mpt-course-english-d10q9.q: ____ the funds been released on time, the project would have finished within budget.
mpt-course-english-d10q9.e: Inverting had replaces if in a formal third conditional.

mpt-course-english-d11q10.q: The accounts ____ externally every year, as the rules require.

mpt-course-english-d11q2.q: Convert to the passive: “The registrar had issued the notice.”
o: The notice was issued by the registrar.
The notice had issued by the registrar.
The notice had been issued by the registrar.
The notice has been issued by the registrar.
mpt-course-english-d11q2.e: Past perfect active becomes had been + participle.

mpt-course-english-d11q3.q: Convert to the passive: “Close the gate at sunset.”
o: The gate was closed at sunset.
The gate is closed at sunset by you.
Let the gate be closed at sunset.
mpt-course-english-d11q3.e: An imperative becomes “Let … be + participle” or “… should be + participle”.

mpt-course-english-d11q4.q: It ____ that the department ignored the earlier warnings.
mpt-course-english-d11q4.e: The impersonal passive of a reporting verb is it is + participle + that.

mpt-course-english-d11q6.q: Which sentence uses the causative correctly?
o: I got repaired my car yesterday.
I had repaired my car by the mechanic.
I had my car repaired yesterday.
I was repaired my car yesterday.
mpt-course-english-d11q6.e: have + object + past participle, in that order.

mpt-course-english-d11q7.q: The applicant ____ a notice of hearing last week.
mpt-course-english-d11q7.e: With a two-object verb, the person may become the passive subject: the applicant was sent a notice.

mpt-course-english-d12q1.q: Report: “Have you seen the notification?” the clerk asked.
o: The clerk asked whether I had seen the notification.
The clerk asked have I seen the notification.
The clerk asked whether had I seen the notification.
The clerk asked that whether I had seen the notification.
mpt-course-english-d12q1.e: Yes-or-no questions take if or whether and statement order.

mpt-course-english-d12q10.q: Which sentence correctly reports “Let us postpone the meeting”?
o: He asked to postpone the meeting that.
He told that they postpone the meeting.
He suggested that the meeting should be postponed.
He said let us postpone the meeting.
mpt-course-english-d12q10.e: Let us is reported with suggest + that-clause or suggest + -ing.

mpt-course-english-d12q3.q: Report: “Do not touch the exhibits,” the guide warned us.
o: The guide warned us that we do not touch the exhibits.
The guide warned us to not touching the exhibits.
The guide warned us not to touch the exhibits.
The guide warned us that do not touch the exhibits.
mpt-course-english-d12q3.e: A negative command becomes not to + infinitive.

mpt-course-english-d12q4.q: She said that she ____ the file the previous day.
mpt-course-english-d12q4.e: A past simple in direct speech backshifts to the past perfect.

mpt-course-english-d12q6.q: Which report keeps the present tense correctly?
o: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
The teacher said that the sun would rise in the east.
mpt-course-english-d12q6.e: A permanent truth is not backshifted.

mpt-course-english-d12q8.q: Report: “Please lend me your notes,” he said to her.
o: He requested her to lend him her notes.
He said her to lend him her notes.
He told her that please lend him her notes.
He requested her that she lends him her notes.
mpt-course-english-d12q8.e: A polite request becomes request/ask + person + to + infinitive.

mpt-course-english-d13q1.q: Find the error: “He is one of (A) the most competent officer (B) in the division (C) this year (D).”
mpt-course-english-d13q1.e: One of the + superlative requires a plural noun: officers.

mpt-course-english-d13q10.q: Only ____ few candidates attempted ____ last question.
mpt-course-english-d13q10.e: A few means some; the last question is identified by the ordinal.

mpt-course-english-d13q4.q: The accused was released from ____ prison after ____ appeal succeeded.
mpt-course-english-d13q4.e: In or from prison as an inmate takes no article; the appeal is the specific one mentioned.

mpt-course-english-d13q5.q: Find the error: “The Pakistan (A) is a member (B) of the United Nations (C) and the Commonwealth (D).”
mpt-course-english-d13q5.e: A single-word country name takes no article; organisation names with of or plural forms do.

mpt-course-english-d13q7.q: It was ____ honour to serve on ____ committee that drafted the policy.
mpt-course-english-d13q7.e: Honour has a silent h; the relative clause identifies which committee.

mpt-course-english-d14q10.q: Which sentence has a clear reference for This?
o: The department delayed the audit for two years. This is unacceptable.
The department delayed the audit for two years. This delay is unacceptable.
This is why the department delayed the audit.
mpt-course-english-d14q10.e: This + a noun names exactly what is being criticised.

mpt-course-english-d14q4.q: She is the scholar ____ work on land reform is most often cited.
mpt-course-english-d14q4.e: Possession requires whose; who’s means who is.

mpt-course-english-d14q6.q: Find the error: “Myself and two colleagues (A) prepared the draft (B) over three days (C) in the secretariat (D).”
mpt-course-english-d14q6.e: A reflexive cannot be a subject: “Two colleagues and I prepared …”.

mpt-course-english-d15q1.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q1.q: Find the error: “Driving through the flooded district (A), the damaged bridges (B) were clearly visible (C) from the road (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q1.e: Bridges do not drive. Name the traveller: “we could clearly see the damaged bridges”.

mpt-course-english-d15q10.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q10.q: Find the error: “He said he would (A) only sign the file (B) after the legal branch (C) had cleared it (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q10.e: The limit is on the timing, not the act: “he would sign the file only after the legal branch had cleared it”.

mpt-course-english-d15q2.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q2.q: Which sentence places the modifier correctly?
o: The department almost has released all the funds.
Almost the department has released all the funds.
The department has released almost all the funds.
The department has almost released all the funds.
mpt-course-english-d15q2.e: Almost limits the quantity, so it belongs beside all the funds.

mpt-course-english-d16q2.q: There is no easy solution ____ the energy crisis.

mpt-course-english-d16q5.q: The new duty had a significant effect ____ import volumes.
mpt-course-english-d16q5.e: Effect on is the fixed partnership; affect is the verb.

mpt-course-english-d16q8.q: He arrived ____ time for the interview but not ____ time to revise his notes.
mpt-course-english-d16q8.e: On time = punctual; in time = early enough for something.

mpt-course-english-d17q1.q: Find the error: “The board suggested (A) to reconsider (B) the eligibility rules (C) before the next cycle (D).”
mpt-course-english-d17q1.e: Suggest takes the gerund: suggested reconsidering.

mpt-course-english-d17q10.q: She managed ____ the file before the office closed.

mpt-course-english-d17q2.q: Which sentence means that he gave up the habit?
o: He stopped in order to smoke.
He has stopped to smoke daily.
He stopped to smoke outside the building.
He stopped smoking two years ago.
mpt-course-english-d17q2.e: stop + -ing means to end an activity; stop + to means to pause in order to do something.

mpt-course-english-d17q3.q: I regret ____ you that your application has been rejected.
mpt-course-english-d17q3.e: regret + to + verb introduces the bad news you are delivering now.

mpt-course-english-d17q4.q: Find the error: “The department denied (A) to have received (B) the representation (C) within the stipulated period (D).”
mpt-course-english-d17q4.e: Deny takes the gerund: denied having received.

mpt-course-english-d17q5.q: ____ the accounts carefully, the auditor identified three irregularities.
mpt-course-english-d17q5.e: The perfect participle marks the earlier of the two actions, and the auditor is the doer of both.

mpt-course-english-d17q7.q: ____ clear rules is easier than enforcing them.
mpt-course-english-d17q7.e: A gerund heads the subject and pairs naturally with the gerund after than.

mpt-course-english-d17q9.q: Which sentence uses the participle correctly?
o: Having written in haste, the note was unclear.
Writing in haste, the note contained three errors.
Written in haste, the note contained three errors.
Written in haste, the officer signed the note.
mpt-course-english-d17q9.e: The note was written in haste, so the past participle correctly describes the note.

mpt-course-english-d18q3.q: His performance in the interview was not so impressive ____ his written papers.
mpt-course-english-d18q3.e: Not so … as is the fixed pattern of negative equality.

mpt-course-english-d18q5.q: The sooner the file is cleared, ____.
mpt-course-english-d18q5.e: The parallel pattern is the sooner … the better.

mpt-course-english-d19q10.q: Find the error: “As the rains failed (A), so the wheat output (B) fell by (C) nine per cent (D).”
mpt-course-english-d19q10.e: As already marks the cause; so must go.

mpt-course-english-d19q2.q: The project was abandoned ____ a shortage of funds.
mpt-course-english-d19q2.e: A noun phrase follows, so a prepositional connector is required.

o: She is responsible not only for revenue but also excise.
She is responsible not only for revenue but also for excise.
She is not only responsible for revenue but also excise.
She not only is responsible for revenue but also for excise.
mpt-course-english-d19q3.e: Each half of the pair is followed by the same structure: for + noun.

mpt-course-english-d19q8.q: The scheme was designed ____ small farmers could obtain credit without collateral.
mpt-course-english-d19q8.e: A clause with its own subject follows, so so that is required.

mpt-course-english-d19q9.q: Which sentence shows contrast between two simultaneous facts?
o: Punjab raised its education budget, therefore Sindh reduced its own.
Punjab raised its education budget, whereas Sindh reduced its own.
Punjab raised its education budget, moreover Sindh reduced its own.
Punjab raised its education budget because Sindh reduced its own.
mpt-course-english-d19q9.e: Whereas marks a direct contrast between two parallel facts.

mpt-course-english-d1q10.q: Find the error: “Decision (A) to postpone the examination (B) was announced (C) on Friday (D).”
mpt-course-english-d1q10.e: A singular countable noun cannot stand alone as a subject. Write “The decision”.

mpt-course-english-d1q2.q: A significant ____ of complaints was received by the ombudsman.
mpt-course-english-d1q2.e: Complaints are countable, so number is correct. Amount belongs with uncountable nouns.

o: She performed well in the interview.
She performed good in the interview.
She performed a good in the interview.
She performed goodly in the interview.
mpt-course-english-d1q3.e: Performed is an action verb, so it needs the adverb well, not the adjective good.

mpt-course-english-d1q5.q: The policy was ____ criticised by independent economists.
mpt-course-english-d1q5.e: The word describes the participle criticised, so an adverb is required.

mpt-course-english-d1q6.q: In which sentence is fund used as a verb?
o: Donors will fund the second phase.
mpt-course-english-d1q6.e: In option B, fund carries the action after the modal will, so it is a verb.

mpt-course-english-d1q8.e: Appear is a linking verb, so the adjective convincing follows it.

mpt-course-english-d1q9.q: The candidate worked ____ throughout the year but ____ took a day of leave.
mpt-course-english-d1q9.e: Hard means with effort; hardly means almost not. The sentence needs one of each, in that order.

mpt-course-english-d20q10.q: Which set of bullet points is parallel?
o: Improving enrolment; training teachers; reducing dropout
Improve enrolment; teacher training; to reduce dropout
Enrolment improvement; train teachers; reducing dropout
Improve enrolment; training teachers; dropout reduction
mpt-course-english-d20q10.e: All three begin with a gerund.

o: Drafting a summary is harder than a note.
To draft a summary is harder than drafting a note.
Drafting a summary is harder than drafting a note.
Drafting a summary is harder than to draft a note.

mpt-course-english-d20q7.q: Find the error: “Candidates must either submit (A) the original degree (B) or they should attach (C) an attested copy (D).”
mpt-course-english-d20q7.e: Either … or must join like with like: “or attach an attested copy”.

o: The section officer examined the file and the deputy secretary approved it.
The file was examined by the section officer and the deputy secretary approved it.
The section officer examined the file and it was approved by the deputy secretary.
The file was examined by the section officer and approved the deputy secretary.
mpt-course-english-d20q8.e: Both clauses stay active, so the sentence reads as one movement.

mpt-course-english-d20q9.q: Find the error: “He is responsible for planning (A), for budgeting (B) and to monitor (C) the annual programme (D).”
mpt-course-english-d20q9.e: The third item must be for monitoring.

mpt-course-english-d21q1.q: Find the error: “The commission performs: (A) four functions (B) — advising, inspecting, (C) reporting and recommending (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q1.e: A colon cannot stand between a verb and its object. Delete it: “The commission performs four functions — advising, inspecting …”.

mpt-course-english-d21q3.q: Find the error: “The delegates came from Lahore, Punjab, (A) Quetta, Balochistan, (B) and Gilgit (C) last Tuesday (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q3.e: Because the items contain internal commas, they must be separated by semicolons: “Lahore, Punjab; Quetta, Balochistan; and Gilgit”.

mpt-course-english-d21q5.q: Find the error: “The tribunal described the delay as, (A) “wholly unexplained” (B) and ordered (C) an inquiry (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q5.e: A partial quotation after as takes no comma.

mpt-course-english-d21q7.q: Find the error: “The scheme failed; (A) although the funds (B) had been released (C) in time (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q7.e: A semicolon cannot precede a dependent clause; a comma or nothing is correct here.

mpt-course-english-d21q9.q: Find the error: “Only one province (A) — Balochistan, (B) was excluded (C) from the scheme (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q9.e: The insertion must close with a second dash, not a comma.

mpt-course-english-d22q2.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q2.q: Find the redundancy: “The committee reviewed (A) the past history (B) of the dispute (C) before deciding (D).”

mpt-course-english-d22q4.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q4.q: Find the redundancy: “Each and every candidate (A) must bring (B) an original (C) identity card (D).”
mpt-course-english-d22q4.e: Each and every says the same thing twice.

mpt-course-english-d22q6.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q6.q: Replace “in the event that the appeal is dismissed”.
o: when there is an appeal dismissal event
at the time of the dismissal of the appeal
mpt-course-english-d22q6.e: If carries the whole meaning in one word.

mpt-course-english-d22q7.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q7.q: Find the redundancy: “The file was returned back (A) to the section (B) on the following (C) Monday (D).”
mpt-course-english-d22q7.e: Return already contains the idea of back.

mpt-course-english-d22q8.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q8.q: Which sentence is both concise and complete?
o: The policy, it is possible to say, has had an effect which is limited.
It may be said that the policy has, to some extent, had some effect.
The policy has had a limited effect.
mpt-course-english-d22q8.e: The qualification survives; the throat-clearing does not.

mpt-course-english-d22q9.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q9.q: Find the wordy phrase: “The department will act (A) at this point in time (B) to reduce (C) the backlog (D).”
mpt-course-english-d22q9.e: At this point in time means now.

mpt-course-english-d23q1.q: Find the error: “The report shows (A) that the scheme’s effect (B) on rural incomes (C) was continual and unbroken (D).”
mpt-course-english-d23q1.e: Continual means repeated with breaks, so it contradicts unbroken. Use continuous.

mpt-course-english-d23q10.q: Which replaces “find out the reason for the delay” formally?
o: figure out why it was late
establish the cause of the delay
get to the bottom of the delay
mpt-course-english-d23q10.e: Establish and cause are the formal equivalents.

mpt-course-english-d23q3.q: From the minister’s silence the press ____ that a decision had already been taken.
mpt-course-english-d23q3.e: The listener infers; the speaker implies.

mpt-course-english-d23q4.q: Find the error: “The committee comprises of (A) seven members (B), three of whom (C) are officials (D).”
mpt-course-english-d23q4.e: Comprise takes no of. Write “comprises seven members” or “is composed of seven members”.

mpt-course-english-d23q9.q: Candidates should ____ précis writing daily; regular ____ is essential.
mpt-course-english-d23q9.e: In British usage practise is the verb and practice the noun.

o: The law was changed six months later. The tribunal reserved judgement.
Six months later the law changed. Judgement had been reserved.
The tribunal reserved judgement. The law was changed by the judgement six months later.
The tribunal reserved judgement. That judgement, delivered six months later, changed the law.
mpt-course-english-d24q1.e: The new element at the end of the first sentence becomes the given at the start of the second.

mpt-course-english-d24q2.q: Find the shift: “A candidate who prepares systematically (A) will find that you retain more (B) and that your revision (C) becomes faster (D).”
mpt-course-english-d24q2.e: The third-person subject shifts to the second person. Keep he, she, they or the candidate throughout.

mpt-course-english-d24q3.q: Which summary noun best continues: “Three districts refused to implement the order.”?
o: This refusal was never formally recorded.
mpt-course-english-d24q3.e: A precise summary noun both links and judges.

mpt-course-english-d24q4.q: Which paragraph opening is a true topic sentence?
o: There are many problems with enforcement.
Enforcement, not legislation, is the binding constraint.
In 2019, the smog emergency was declared.
mpt-course-english-d24q4.e: It states one arguable claim the paragraph can support.

mpt-course-english-d24q6.q: Which sentence uses ellipsis correctly for concision?
o: The first proposal was costly; the second, less so.
The first proposal was costly; the second proposal was less costly than the first proposal.
The first proposal was costly, the second was costly less.
The first proposal costly; second less.
mpt-course-english-d24q6.e: The repeated words are understood and need not be written.

mpt-course-english-d24q7.q: Which is the weaker use of a connector?
o: The funds lapsed, so the work stopped.
Because the funds lapsed, the work stopped.
The funds lapsed. The work therefore stopped.
The funds lapsed. Moreover, the work stopped.
mpt-course-english-d24q7.e: Moreover claims addition where the real relationship is cause and effect.

mpt-course-english-d24q9.q: Find the vague reference: “The department ignored two reminders and missed the deadline (A). This (B) was reported to the secretary (C) in writing (D).”
mpt-course-english-d24q9.e: This could mean the reminders, the omission or the delay. Write “This failure” or name it.

mpt-course-english-d25q10.q: Find the error: “The government will analyze (A) the programme (B) and publish (C) its defence (D) of the policy.”
mpt-course-english-d25q10.e: The rest of the sentence uses British spelling, so analyse is required. Keep one system throughout.

mpt-course-english-d25q5.q: An ____ economist warned that a collapse was ____.
mpt-course-english-d25q5.e: Eminent means distinguished; imminent means about to happen.

mpt-course-english-d25q8.q: The two candidates differed on many points; the ____ was better prepared.
mpt-course-english-d25q8.e: Latter means the second of two; later refers to time.

mpt-course-english-d26q1.q: Find the error: “The number of applications (A) received this year (B) have exceeded (C) all previous records (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q1.e: Pass 1: the head noun is number, which is singular — has exceeded.

mpt-course-english-d26q10.q: Two corrections are possible for “If I would have known, I would have informed you.” Which changes fewer words?
o: If I had known, I would have informed you.
Had I known, I would have informed you.
Knowing that, I would have informed you.
I would have informed you if I had been aware.
mpt-course-english-d26q10.e: Replacing would have with had changes two words and keeps the structure.

mpt-course-english-d26q2.q: Which is the minimum correction of “The quality of the answers were disappointing”?
o: The quality of the answers was disappointing.
The answers were disappointing in quality.
The answers disappointed in their quality.
mpt-course-english-d26q2.e: One verb form is at fault; nothing else moves.

mpt-course-english-d26q3.q: Find the error: “She has been working (A) in this department (B) since the last (C) five years (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q3.e: A duration takes for, not since the last: “for the last five years”.

mpt-course-english-d26q5.q: Find the error: “Neither the clerk (A) nor the officers (B) was aware (C) of the change (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q5.e: Nor points the verb at the nearer subject, officers, so were is required.

mpt-course-english-d26q6.q: Which is the minimum correction of “He suggested to postpone the meeting”?
o: He proposed that the meeting be postponed.
He wanted to postpone the meeting.
He said the meeting should be postponed.
mpt-course-english-d26q6.e: Only the form after suggested is wrong; one word changes.

mpt-course-english-d26q7.q: Find the error: “The population of Karachi (A) is greater (B) than Lahore (C) by several million (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q7.e: Compare like with like: “than that of Lahore”. Two words are inserted, and nothing else moves.

mpt-course-english-d26q9.q: Find the error: “Having reviewed the file (A), a decision (B) was taken (C) to close the case (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q9.e: A decision did not review the file. The minimum repair names the doer: “the officer took a decision”.

mpt-course-english-d2q3.q: Improving literacy rates in rural districts ____ sustained funding.
mpt-course-english-d2q3.e: The whole -ing phrase is one singular subject.

mpt-course-english-d2q5.q: Which group of words is a complete sentence?
o: Although the budget was approved in March.
The budget approved in March by the assembly.
The budget was approved in March.
Approving the budget in March despite objections.
mpt-course-english-d2q5.e: Only option C has a subject and a finite verb and does not begin with a subordinator.

mpt-course-english-d2q6.q: What the tribunal decided in those two cases ____ still disputed.
mpt-course-english-d2q6.e: The subject is the whole what-clause, which counts as one singular idea.

mpt-course-english-d2q8.q: In “The board declared the contract void”, what is void?
mpt-course-english-d2q8.e: Void describes the object contract, so it is an object complement.

mpt-course-english-d2q9.q: Neither the chairman nor the members ____ willing to sign.
mpt-course-english-d2q9.e: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, members.

mpt-course-english-d3q1.q: Find the error: “Even though (A) the department issued a clarification (B), but the confusion (C) continued for weeks (D).”
mpt-course-english-d3q1.e: Even though and but both mark contrast. Delete but.

mpt-course-english-d3q4.q: Find the error: “Because of (A) the applicant had submitted (B) the wrong form (C), the request was rejected (D).”
mpt-course-english-d3q4.e: A full clause follows, so because is required, not because of.

mpt-course-english-d3q5.q: Which group of words is a fragment?
o: The deadline, which passed last Monday, was final.
Since the deadline passed last Monday.
mpt-course-english-d3q5.e: Since makes the clause dependent, so it cannot stand alone.

mpt-course-english-d3q6.q: In “The report shows that enforcement has failed”, the that-clause works as
mpt-course-english-d3q6.e: It answers “shows what?”, so it is a noun clause working as the object.

mpt-course-english-d3q7.q: Find the error: “The villages, that were worst affected (A) by the floods (B), received relief (C) three weeks late (D).”
mpt-course-english-d3q7.e: Use which after a comma. That never introduces a non-defining clause.

mpt-course-english-d3q8.q: ____ the tribunal reserved its judgement, the parties waited outside.
mpt-course-english-d3q8.e: A clause follows, so a subordinator is needed; during and despite take nouns.

mpt-course-english-d5q4.q: Attached to the application ____ three certificates.
mpt-course-english-d5q4.e: The subject, certificates, follows the verb and is plural.

mpt-course-english-d5q6.e: Most takes its number from evidence, which is uncountable and singular.

mpt-course-english-d5q9.q: Either the secretary or his deputies ____ to attend the briefing.
mpt-course-english-d5q9.e: The nearer subject, deputies, is plural.

mpt-course-english-d6q4.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
mpt-course-english-d6q4.q: Find the error: “In 1947 (A) Pakistan (B) gained independence, (C) and adopted a new flag (D).”
mpt-course-english-d6q4.e: “adopted a new flag” has no subject of its own, so no comma is needed before and.

mpt-course-english-d7q10.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
mpt-course-english-d7q10.q: The file ____ four annexures and a covering note.
mpt-course-english-d7q10.e: Contain is stative and takes the simple form.

mpt-course-english-d7q4.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
mpt-course-english-d7q4.q: The novel ____ the collapse of a landed family in colonial Bengal.
mpt-course-english-d7q4.e: Discussion of a literary text uses the present simple.

mpt-course-english-d8q10.q: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
o: The commission has met three times yesterday.
The commission has met three times in 2019.
The commission has met three times last month.
The commission has met three times this month.
mpt-course-english-d8q10.e: This month is an unfinished period, so the present perfect fits.

mpt-course-english-d8q4.q: Prices ____ steadily since the imposition of the new duty.
mpt-course-english-d8q4.e: Since requires a perfect tense, and rise is the intransitive verb.

mpt-course-english-d8q6.q: How long ____ you ____ for the result?
mpt-course-english-d8q6.e: How long with an activity continuing to now takes the present perfect continuous.

mpt-course-english-d8q9.q: The file ____ on the table where the clerk had left it.
mpt-course-english-d8q9.e: Lie (to rest) has the past form lay; laid belongs to lay (to place something).

mpt-course-english-d9q1.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q1.q: Find the error: “If the assembly (A) will pass the bill (B), the president (C) will sign it (D).”
mpt-course-english-d9q1.e: The if-clause takes the present simple: if the assembly passes the bill.

mpt-course-english-d9q10.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q10.q: She promised that she ____ the documents the following day.
mpt-course-english-d9q10.e: Will backshifts to would after a past reporting verb.

mpt-course-english-d9q3.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q3.q: Which sentence describes a fixed arrangement?
o: We will meet the registrar sometime.
We are meeting the registrar at eleven tomorrow.
mpt-course-english-d9q3.e: The present continuous with a stated time marks a fixed arrangement.

mpt-course-english-d9q5.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q5.q: This time next week the candidates ____ the compulsory papers.
mpt-course-english-d9q5.e: An action in progress at a stated future point takes the future continuous.

mpt-course-english-d9q7.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q7.q: The teacher explained that light ____ faster than sound.
mpt-course-english-d9q7.e: A scientific truth keeps the present tense after a past reporting verb.

mpt-course-english-d9q8.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q8.q: Find the error: “By the time the inquiry concludes (A), the officer (B) will retire (C) from service (D).”
mpt-course-english-d9q8.e: By the time + a future point requires the future perfect: will have retired.

mpt-course-english-d9q9.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q9.q: Which sentence shows an intention formed before speaking?
o: I would apply for the post.
I will apply for the post.
I am going to apply for the post.
mpt-course-english-d9q9.e: Going to signals a plan already decided.

mpt-current-expanded-070.q: From which regional group was the President of UNGA 81 due to be elected under rotation?
mpt-current-expanded-070.e: The established rotation allocated the election to the Asia-Pacific Group.

mpt-current-verified-012.q: The WHO’s 2026 negotiations on a key annex to its Pandemic Agreement concerned which mechanism?
mpt-current-verified-012.e: WHO member states were negotiating the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing annex.

mpt-past-papers-352.q: If BAT is coded as 283, CAT is coded as 383 and ARE is coded as 801, then the code for BETTER is:
mpt-past-papers-352.e: From the codes B=2, A=8, T=3, C=3, R=0 and E=1, so BETTER = 2-1-3-3-1-0 = 213310.
