pakistan-affairs-1394.q: When did Eighth Constitutional Amendment take place?
pakistan-affairs-1394.e: The Eighth Amendment, passed under General Zia-ul-Haq's government, became law on 11 November 1985 and gave the President power to dissolve the National Assembly under Article 58(2)(b).

o: Strengthening bonds with Muslim world and promoting international peace
Subject-matter of Federal and Provincial laws
The Objectives Resolution to form part of substantive provisions
pakistan-affairs-1558.e: Article 2A, inserted in 1985, is titled 'The Objectives Resolution to form part of substantive provisions' and makes the Objectives Resolution an operative part of the Constitution.

pakistan-affairs-1606.e: Article 19A, added by the Eighteenth Amendment (2010), is titled 'Right to information' and gives every citizen access to information on matters of public importance.

pakistan-affairs-3054.q: The Picture on the back of 10 Rupee Pakistani Note
pakistan-affairs-3054.e: The reverse of Pakistan's current green Rs 10 note shows Bab-e-Khyber, the gateway at the Khyber Pass.

pakistan-affairs-3056.q: When Utility Stores Corporation of Pakistan (Pvt.) Limited established?
pakistan-affairs-3056.e: Utility Stores Corporation was set up in 1971 to sell essential goods to the public at controlled prices.

pakistan-affairs-3073.q: Where is the tomb of Mughal Emperor Jahangir?
pakistan-affairs-3073.e: Emperor Jahangir's tomb stands at Shahdara Bagh on the bank of the Ravi in Lahore.

pakistan-affairs-3075.q: Which country is called “land of pure people”?
pakistan-affairs-3075.e: 'Pakistan' literally means 'land of the pure' (pak = pure, stan = land).

pakistan-affairs-3095.q: Headquarter of Pakistan NAVY is in?
pakistan-affairs-3095.e: Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is located in Islamabad, though the main fleet is based in Karachi.

pakistan-affairs-3102.q: How many High Courts of Pakistan are there?
pakistan-affairs-3102.e: Pakistan has five High Courts: Lahore, Sindh, Peshawar, Balochistan and Islamabad.

pakistan-affairs-3112.q: Who was the first Secretary General of Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3112.e: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was appointed the first Secretary General of Pakistan in 1947 and later became Prime Minister.

pakistan-affairs-3118.q: Dr Abdus Slam was born in which city of Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3118.e: Nobel laureate physicist Dr Abdus Salam was born in 1926 in Jhang, Punjab.

pakistan-affairs-3148.q: Which of the following city of Pakistan hosts IDEAS (International defence exhibition and seminar) since it’s inauguration?
pakistan-affairs-3148.e: The IDEAS defence exhibition has been held at the Karachi Expo Centre since its first edition in 2000.

pakistan-affairs-3149.q: The severity of 2005 earthquake in Pakistan on Richter scale was?
pakistan-affairs-3149.e: The 8 October 2005 Kashmir earthquake had a magnitude of 7.6.

pakistan-affairs-3163.q: Which is the national bird of Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3163.e: The Chukar partridge (Chakor) is the national bird of Pakistan.

pakistan-affairs-3190.e: Pakistan formally recognised Bangladesh on 22 February 1974, during the OIC summit in Lahore.

pakistan-affairs-3199.e: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which corresponded to 27 Ramadan 1366 AH.

pakistan-affairs-3237.q: How many time has Queen Elizabeth visited Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3237.e: Queen Elizabeth II visited Pakistan twice, in 1961 and in 1997.

pakistan-affairs-3241.q: Blind dolphins are found in which river of Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3241.e: The blind Indus River dolphin is found only in the Indus River system of Pakistan.

pakistan-affairs-3301.q: CPEC connect the deep-sea Pakistani ports of Gwadar and Karachi to which province of China?
pakistan-affairs-3301.e: CPEC runs from Gwadar to Kashgar in China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

pakistan-affairs-3318.q: Minar-E-Pakistan was designed by which Russian born Pakistani architect?
pakistan-affairs-3318.e: Minar-e-Pakistan was designed by the Russian-born Pakistani architect Nasreddin Murat-Khan.

pakistan-affairs-3333.q: Peace Pipeline is another name of _____ pipeline.
pakistan-affairs-3333.e: The Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline (originally Iran-Pakistan-India) is popularly called the Peace Pipeline.

pakistan-affairs-3344.q: Tear Lake also known as Ansoo Lake is located in which valley of Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3344.e: Ansoo (Tear) Lake, named for its teardrop shape, lies in the Kaghan Valley near Malika Parbat.

pakistan-affairs-3396.q: Who is the Civilian Commander-In-Chief of Pakistan Armed forces?
pakistan-affairs-3396.e: Under Article 243 of the Constitution, the supreme command of the Armed Forces vests in the President.

pakistan-affairs-3399.q: Who was Prime Minister of Pakistan on 2nd December 1988?
pakistan-affairs-3399.e: Benazir Bhutto took oath as Prime Minister on 2 December 1988 after the 1988 general elections.

pakistan-affairs-3413.q: Pakistan's first "Space Rocket" was launched in 1962. What was its name?
pakistan-affairs-3413.e: Rehbar-I, launched by SUPARCO from Sonmiani in June 1962, was Pakistan's first rocket.

pakistan-affairs-342.s: Muslim Reform, Education and Political Awakening
pakistan-affairs-342.q: When did Creation of Eastern Bengal and Assam take place?
pakistan-affairs-342.e: The province of Eastern Bengal and Assam was created by the Partition of Bengal in 1905.

pakistan-affairs-3451.q: Name of range which separates China from Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3451.e: The Karakoram range, crossed by the Khunjerab Pass, forms the border between Pakistan and China.

pakistan-affairs-3459.q: At the time of Independence which community was in majority in the state of Kashmir?
pakistan-affairs-3459.e: At independence Jammu and Kashmir was a Muslim-majority state ruled by a Hindu Dogra Maharaja.

pakistan-affairs-3501.q: Which of the following air company was the first to operate in Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3501.e: Orient Airways, founded in 1946 at Jinnah's encouragement, was the first airline to operate in Pakistan and later merged into PIA.

pakistan-affairs-3504.q: When did PAKISTAN became a member of Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
pakistan-affairs-3504.e: Pakistan became a full member of the SCO at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.

pakistan-affairs-3525.q: When Decimal System was introduced in Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3525.e: Pakistan switched to decimal coinage on 1 January 1961, dividing the rupee into 100 paisa.

pakistan-affairs-3536.q: When did Chouhdry Rehmat Ali introduced the term Pakistan in his pamphlet?
pakistan-affairs-3536.e: Choudhry Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakstan' in his pamphlet 'Now or Never' of January 1933.

pakistan-affairs-3550.q: During Kalhora regime the__________ was official language of Sindh.
pakistan-affairs-3550.e: Persian was the official and court language of Sindh under the Kalhora rulers.

pakistan-affairs-3612.q: The first operational motorway in Pakistan named?
pakistan-affairs-3612.e: The M-2 Lahore-Islamabad motorway, opened in 1997, was Pakistan's first operational motorway.

pakistan-affairs-3613.q: The first Pakistani to reach the North Pole?
pakistan-affairs-3613.e: Namira Salim became the first Pakistani to reach the North Pole, in April 2007.

pakistan-affairs-3622.q: With which country Pakistan has shortest boundary?
pakistan-affairs-3622.e: Pakistan's border with China (about 500-600 km) is shorter than its borders with Iran, Afghanistan and India.

pakistan-affairs-3741.q: The area with lowest rainfall in Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3741.e: Nokkundi in Chagai, Balochistan, receives the lowest average rainfall in Pakistan.

pakistan-affairs-3773.q: The____Moterway connects the cities of Hyderabad and Karachi in the Sindh
pakistan-affairs-3773.e: The M-9 motorway links Karachi and Hyderabad in Sindh.

pakistan-affairs-3783.q: What was name of Ubedullah sindhi before accepting of Islam?
pakistan-affairs-3783.e: Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi was born a Sikh named Buta Singh and took the name Ubaidullah on converting to Islam.

pakistan-affairs-3799.q: When did Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah born?
pakistan-affairs-3799.e: Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.

pakistan-affairs-3800.q: When did state Kalat joined Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3800.e: The Khan of Kalat signed the instrument of accession to Pakistan on 27 March 1948.

pakistan-affairs-3804.q: When Pakistan National Highways & Motorway Police was established?
pakistan-affairs-3804.e: The National Highways and Motorway Police was established in 1997, when the M-2 motorway opened.

pakistan-affairs-3805.e: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (later CENTO) in 1955.

pakistan-affairs-3806.q: When Pakistani Rupee was delinked from USD?
pakistan-affairs-3806.e: On 8 January 1982 Pakistan delinked the rupee from the US dollar and adopted a managed float.

pakistan-affairs-3807.q: When Quaid e Azam left Congress?
pakistan-affairs-3807.e: Jinnah left the Indian National Congress in 1920, opposing Gandhi's non-cooperation movement at the Nagpur session.

pakistan-affairs-3808.q: When T.V Transmission was started in the Pakistan?
pakistan-affairs-3808.e: Pakistan Television began transmission from Lahore on 26 November 1964.

pakistan-affairs-464.q: When did Morley-Minto Reforms take place?
pakistan-affairs-464.e: The Indian Councils Act 1909, known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

pakistan-affairs-545.q: When did Moplah uprising take place?
pakistan-affairs-545.e: The Moplah (Mappila) uprising broke out in Malabar in 1921, during the Khilafat movement.

pakistan-history-538.q: Indian Independence Act’ was enforced on?
pakistan-history-538.e: The Indian Independence Act 1947 set 15 August 1947 as the appointed day from which India and Pakistan became dominions.

pakistan-history-596.q: Last emperor to sit on peacock throne was?
pakistan-history-596.e: Muhammad Shah was the last Mughal emperor to sit on the Peacock Throne; Nadir Shah carried it off to Persia in 1739.

pakistan-history-606.q: The Railway workshop of Mughalpura is situated in?
pakistan-history-606.e: The Mughalpura Railway Workshops, among the largest in South Asia, are in Lahore.

science-2370.q: Which structure contains most genetic material in a eukaryotic cell?
science-2370.e: Most eukaryotic DNA is enclosed within the nucleus.

science-2371.q: Which cellular structure primarily assembles ribosomal subunits?
science-2371.e: The nucleolus primarily assembles ribosomal subunits.

science-2374.q: Which cellular structure primarily synthesises lipids and detoxifies chemicals?
science-2374.e: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum primarily synthesises lipids and detoxifies chemicals.

science-2376.q: Which cellular structure primarily performs acidic intracellular digestion?
science-2376.e: The lysosome primarily performs acidic intracellular digestion.

science-2377.q: Which cellular structure primarily oxidises fatty acids and detoxifies peroxide?
science-2377.e: The peroxisome primarily oxidises fatty acids and detoxifies peroxide.

science-2378.q: Which cellular structure primarily generates most aerobic ATP?
science-2378.e: The mitochondrion primarily generates most aerobic ATP.

science-2379.q: Which cellular structure primarily performs photosynthesis?

science-2380.q: Which cellular structure primarily maintains plant-cell turgor?
science-2380.e: The central vacuole primarily maintains plant-cell turgor.

science-2381.q: Which cellular structure primarily organises microtubules in many animal cells?
science-2381.e: The centrosome primarily organises microtubules in many animal cells.

science-2770.q: Which tissue transports water upward in vascular plants?
science-2770.e: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals from roots.

science-2851.q: Which biological agents are prokaryotes distinct from bacteria?
science-2851.e: archaea are prokaryotes distinct from bacteria.

science-2853.q: Which biological agents are mostly unicellular eukaryotic heterotrophs?
science-2853.e: protozoa are mostly unicellular eukaryotic heterotrophs.

science-2855.q: Which biological agents are small infectious RNA molecules?
science-2855.e: viroids are small infectious RNA molecules.

science-2856.q: Which biological agents are infectious misfolded proteins?

science-2857.q: Which named group of bacteria performs oxygenic photosynthesis?

science-2891.q: Which cells directly kill many virus-infected host cells?
science-2891.e: Cytotoxic T cells recognise antigen on MHC I and induce target-cell death.

science-3175.q: Which planet has the Solar System’s most prominent ring system?
science-3175.e: Saturn is the most prominent ring system.

science-3180.q: Which listed Solar System body is an icy moon of Jupiter with strong evidence for a subsurface ocean?
science-3180.e: Europa is the icy moon with evidence for a subsurface ocean.

science-3251.q: Which event occurs when Earth passes directly between the Sun and the Moon so that Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon?
science-3251.e: That geometry defines a lunar eclipse.

science-3254.q: Which tidal condition occurs when the Sun, Earth and Moon are nearly aligned?
science-3254.e: That geometry defines a spring tides.

science-3255.q: Which event occurs when the solar and lunar tidal forces are near right angles?
science-3255.e: That geometry defines a neap tides.

science-3257.q: Which event occurs when the Northern Hemisphere tilts most away from the Sun?
science-3257.e: That geometry defines a northern winter solstice.

science-3261.q: Which event occurs when the Moon is nearest Earth in its orbit?

science-3330.q: The Sun’s energy is generated mainly by
science-3330.e: Hydrogen fusion into helium powers the main-sequence Sun.

science-4010.q: Which seismic wave cannot travel through a liquid?
science-4010.e: Shear waves require rigidity, which liquids lack.

science-4290.q: The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth
o: Warmer than it would be without infrared-absorbing gases
science-4290.e: Greenhouse gases reduce outgoing infrared energy and warm the surface–troposphere system.

science-4778.q: The lifespan of Red Blood Cells is _____ days.
science-4778.e: Human red blood cells live about 120 days before the spleen and liver remove them.

science-4782.e: The Sun is a star, a ball of hot gas that produces its own light and energy through nuclear fusion.

science-4784.q: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust
science-4784.e: Oxygen is the most abundant element in Earth's crust, making up about 46% of it by mass, mostly in silicate minerals.

science-4787.q: The most densest substance on the Earth is
science-4787.e: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, at about 22.6 g/cm3, denser than platinum, copper or steel.

science-4790.q: Which from the following is true for "Sound"?
o: Sound cannot travel through a vaccum
science-4790.e: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a medium, so it travels through solids, liquids and gases but not through a vacuum.

science-4798.q: The planet that moves round the Sun at the highest speed is?
science-4798.e: Mercury is closest to the Sun and feels the strongest pull of its gravity, so it has the highest orbital speed, about 47 km/s.

science-4820.q: The natural fats and oils are composed of
science-4820.e: Fats and oils are esters of glycerol and fatty acids, so they contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

science-4831.q: The device used to measure movements of the heart is
science-4831.e: A cardiograph (for example an electrocardiograph) records the activity and movements of the heart.

science-4872.q: The thickest layer of the Earth is
science-4872.e: The mantle is about 2,900 km thick, which makes it the thickest of Earth's layers.

science-4918.q: The organisms that can make their own food are called
science-4918.e: Producers such as green plants make their own food from carbon dioxide and water by photosynthesis.

science-4947.q: The structure that is absent in animal cell
science-4947.e: Plant cells have a cell wall but animal cells have only a cell membrane; animal cells do have a nucleus, mitochondria and centrioles.

science-4973.q: The foetus is protected from the mechanical damage by the
science-4973.e: Amniotic fluid surrounds the foetus inside the amniotic sac and cushions it against shocks and mechanical injury.

science-5010.q: A system of wind in which wind blows spirally toward the center of low pressure is called?
science-5010.e: A cyclone is a system of winds that spiral inward toward a centre of low pressure.

science-5011.q: International Energy Agency (IEA) was founded in year?
science-5011.e: The International Energy Agency was set up in November 1974, after the 1973 oil crisis.

science-5012.q: The headquarter of organizations for the prohibition of chemical weapons?
science-5012.e: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons has its headquarters in The Hague, in the Netherlands (Nederland).

science-5014.q: How many rows and columns are in the modern Periodic Table?
science-5014.e: The modern periodic table has 18 vertical columns (groups) and 7 horizontal rows (periods).

science-5026.q: Which animal has the largest brain in the world?
science-5026.e: The sperm whale has the largest brain of any animal, weighing about 7-8 kg.

science-5032.q: Which animal has the largest ears of any animal in the planet?
science-5032.e: The African elephant has the largest ears of any animal, and it uses them to give off body heat.

science-5034.q: What are Columns in Periodic table called?
science-5034.e: The vertical columns of the periodic table are called groups; the horizontal rows are called periods.

science-5064.q: The only organ of UN which has the headquarters outside New York is?
science-5064.e: The International Court of Justice sits in The Hague, Netherlands, while the UN's other principal organs are based in New York.

science-5065.q: Where is the headquarter of International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) located?
science-5065.e: The International Atomic Energy Agency has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria.

science-5080.q: The chemical that is used in making artificial rain is?
science-5080.e: Silver iodide is used in cloud seeding because its crystal structure resembles ice, so water droplets freeze on it and form precipitation.

science-5089.q: Which animal is depicted on the logo of WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature)?
science-5089.e: The WWF logo shows a giant panda, based on Chi Chi, a panda at London Zoo.

science-5119.q: What is the smallest unit of heredity?
science-5119.e: A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a trait, which makes it the basic unit of heredity.

science-5120.q: Which of the following is a currency of Body cells?
science-5120.e: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the cell's energy currency, storing and releasing energy for cellular processes.

science-5121.q: Which of the following is not an enzyme?
science-5121.e: Secretin is a hormone released by the duodenum that makes the pancreas secrete bicarbonate, while pepsin and chymotrypsin are digestive enzymes.

science-5126.q: Alzheimer's disease in human beings is characterized by the degeneration of _____
science-5126.e: Alzheimer's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder in which brain nerve cells (neurons) degenerate and die, causing memory loss.

science-5144.e: Mumps is caused by the mumps virus, a paramyxovirus, and it causes swelling of the parotid salivary glands.

science-5145.q: What do you understand by disease "Insomnia"?
science-5145.e: Insomnia is a sleep disorder in which a person persistently has difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

science-5146.q: What does TCM stand for in medical terms?
science-5146.e: In medicine, TCM stands for Traditional Chinese Medicine, which includes practices such as acupuncture and herbal remedies.

science-5148.q: Which form of drug abuse involves most risk of infection with the HIV (AIDS) virus?
science-5148.e: Injecting heroin with shared needles can pass on HIV through infected blood, so it carries the highest HIV risk of the options.

science-5149.q: Which of the following disease is spread by Fleas?
science-5149.e: Murine (endemic) typhus is transmitted to humans by rat fleas, whereas yellow fever is spread by mosquitoes.

science-5150.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by virus?
science-5150.e: Smallpox was caused by the variola virus, whereas cholera and tuberculosis are bacterial and malaria is caused by a protozoan.

science-5151.q: Which of the following is not a contagious disease?
science-5151.e: Hysteria is a psychological condition and is not caused by an infectious agent, so it cannot pass from person to person.

science-5152.q: Which part of the body is attacked by "Gingivitis" disease?
science-5152.e: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, usually caused by plaque building up on the teeth.

science-5175.q: How many bones in our body?
science-5175.e: An adult human skeleton normally has 206 bones, because many bones present at birth fuse together.

science-5176.q: How many chambers are in the human heart?
science-5176.e: The human heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

science-5178.q: How many hearts an Octopus has?
science-5178.e: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood through the gills and one pumps it to the rest of the body.

science-5179.q: How many Number of eyes found in Earthworm?
science-5179.e: Earthworms have no eyes; they detect light with photoreceptor cells in their skin.

science-5248.q: What is the name of the biggest part of human brain?
science-5248.e: The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain and controls thought, voluntary movement and the senses.

science-5251.q: What is the weight of the average human brain?
science-5251.e: An average adult human brain weighs about 1.2 to 1.4 kg.

science-5253.q: Where is the uvula located in human body?
science-5253.e: The uvula is the small fleshy flap hanging from the back of the soft palate at the top of the throat.

science-5254.q: Which are the largest of the white blood cells?
science-5254.e: Monocytes are the largest white blood cells, and in tissues they develop into macrophages.

science-5268.q: Which Part of the Brain Regulates Body Temperature?
science-5268.e: The hypothalamus acts as the body's thermostat, controlling sweating, shivering and blood flow to keep body temperature steady.

science-5269.q: Which part of the Camera is analogue to the retina in the human eye?
science-5269.e: In a camera the image is focused onto the film (or sensor), just as the eye's lens focuses the image onto the retina.

science-5270.q: Which term describes the emission of light by a living organism?
science-5270.e: Bioluminescence is the production of light by living organisms, such as fireflies, through a chemical reaction involving luciferin.

science-5291.q: The contraction and expansion of the movement of the walls of the food pipe after entering the slightly digested food is known as _____ movement
science-5291.e: Peristalsis is the wave-like contraction and relaxation of the oesophagus walls that pushes food down to the stomach.

science-5303.q: What is the one of the other name of Vitamin "A"?
science-5303.e: Vitamin A is also called retinol, while thiamin is B1, riboflavin is B2 and ascorbic acid is vitamin C.

science-5304.q: Which of the following disease affects the skin?
science-5304.e: Pellagra, caused by a lack of niacin (vitamin B3), produces dermatitis, a skin inflammation, as one of its main symptoms.

science-5305.q: Which of the following have maximum calorific value?
science-5305.e: Fats give about 9 kcal per gram, more than twice the roughly 4 kcal per gram from proteins or carbohydrates.

science-5308.q: Which of the following is nutritional deficiency disease?
science-5308.e: Pellagra is caused by a lack of niacin (vitamin B3) in the diet, while albinism is genetic and rabies is viral.

science-5334.q: Phosphorus is an essential component of one of the following biological molecules
science-5334.e: Phosphorus forms the phosphate groups in the sugar-phosphate backbone of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

science-5341.q: What is the common name for the drug acetyl salicylic acid?
science-5341.e: Acetylsalicylic acid is the chemical name of aspirin, a common painkiller and anti-inflammatory drug.

science-5342.e: Gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid and has a pH of about 1.5-3.5, much lower than that of bile, saliva or pancreatic juice.

science-5343.q: Who was the surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery in 1865?
science-5343.e: Joseph Lister introduced antiseptic surgery in 1865 by using carbolic acid (phenol) to sterilise wounds and instruments.

science-5398.q: The chemical name of quartz is
science-5398.e: Quartz is a mineral made of silicon dioxide (SiO2).

science-5405.q: The half life of a radioactive element is 8-days. How long it take to reduce it from 10 mg to 5 mg?
science-5405.e: Half-life is the time for half of a radioactive sample to decay, so going from 10 mg to 5 mg takes one half-life, 8 days.

science-5416.q: The number of electrons of a neutral atom is automatically known if one knows the?
science-5416.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, and the atomic number is the number of protons.

science-5436.q: Which law states that the volume of a given amount of gas held at constant pressure is directly proportional to the Kelvin temperature?
science-5436.e: Charles's law states that at constant pressure the volume of a fixed amount of gas is directly proportional to its absolute (Kelvin) temperature.

science-5437.q: Which natural element has the highest melting point?
science-5437.e: Tungsten melts at about 3,422 °C, the highest melting point of any metal and far above silver, copper or iron.

science-5441.q: Which of the following is a component of soap?
science-5441.e: Soap is made by saponification of fats, and sodium stearate, the sodium salt of stearic acid, is a typical soap.

science-5442.q: Which of the following is not a chemical reaction?
science-5442.e: Turning water into steam is a physical change of state, because no new substance is formed.

science-5450.q: Which one of the following is not a radioactive element?
science-5450.e: Cadmium's natural isotopes are stable, while uranium, radium and thorium are radioactive.

science-5451.q: Which one of the following is the main culprit in the thinning of Ozone layer in the earth's stratosphere?
science-5451.e: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere, and these break down ozone molecules.

science-5485.q: _____ is the "Work done in moving a unit charge between two points in an electric circuit"?
science-5485.e: Potential difference (voltage) is the work done in moving a unit charge between two points, measured in volts (joules per coulomb).

science-5495.q: Which is least Conductor of Electricity among the following?
science-5495.e: Dry wood is an electrical insulator, whereas copper and iron are metallic conductors and ordinary water with dissolved salts conducts better than dry wood.

science-5523.q: Which of these is NOT a form of energy?
science-5523.e: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of particles, not a form of energy itself; heat, light and electricity are forms of energy.

science-5547.q: The average speed of a moving object during a given interval of time is always
o: one-half its speed at the end of the interval
its acceleration multiplied by the time interval
the magnitude of its average velocity over the interval
the distance covered during the time interval divided by the time interval
science-5547.e: Average speed is defined as total distance travelled divided by the time taken; it equals the magnitude of average velocity only when motion is in a straight line without reversal.

science-5555.q: What prevents the earth's atmosphere from drifting away into space?
science-5555.e: The Earth's gravity pulls the gases of the atmosphere towards the planet and prevents them from escaping into space.

science-5558.q: Which of the following has the highest energy?
science-5558.e: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and highest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum, so their photons carry the most energy.

science-5559.q: Which of these is NOT an example of a renewable energy source?
science-5559.e: Coal is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replenished on a human timescale, while hydro, wind and solar energy are renewable.

science-5572.q: Magnifying power of a simple microscope can be increased by?
o: Decreasing focal length of the lens
increasing focal length of the lens
science-5572.e: The magnifying power of a simple microscope is M = 1 + D/f, so a lens of shorter focal length gives greater magnification.

science-5589.e: A photometer is an instrument used to measure the intensity of light (luminous intensity or illuminance).

science-5591.q: When white light is passed through a prism, it splits into _____ colours.
science-5591.e: White light passing through a prism disperses into seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red (VIBGYOR).

science-5593.q: Which among the following types of lenses are prescribed by doctors for a patient suffering from astigmatism?
science-5593.e: Astigmatism is caused by unequal curvature of the cornea or lens, and it is corrected with cylindrical lenses that focus light differently in different planes.

science-5594.q: Which lenses are used by people having short- sightedness?
science-5594.e: In short-sightedness (myopia) the image forms in front of the retina, so a concave (diverging) lens is used to correct it.

science-5595.q: Which of the following has the largest wavelength?
science-5595.e: Infrared radiation has a longer wavelength than visible light, ultraviolet and X-rays, which lie at progressively shorter wavelengths.

science-5596.q: Who first measured the velocity of light?
science-5596.e: The Danish astronomer Ole Roemer made the first measurement of the speed of light in 1676 by observing the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io; Galileo's earlier attempt failed.

science-5609.q: What is the molecular formula for Ammonia?
science-5609.e: Ammonia consists of one nitrogen atom bonded to three hydrogen atoms, so its formula is NH3.

science-5611.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of volume?
science-5611.e: In the SI system the unit of length is the metre, so the unit of volume is the cubic metre (m³).

science-5612.q: Which one of the following is not a unit of distance?
science-5612.e: The foot-candle is a unit of illuminance (light falling on a surface), whereas the astronomical unit, parsec and light year are units of distance.

science-5633.q: The deficiency of Vitamin D causes which disease in children?
science-5633.e: Vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium and phosphorus; its deficiency in children softens the bones and causes rickets.

science-5636.q: The sun's energy is produced by which process?
science-5636.e: In the Sun's core hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium, and this nuclear fusion releases the Sun's energy.

urdu-language-774.q: “صلح” کے قریب ترین معنی کون سے ہیں؟
urdu-language-774.e: «صلح» کا مطلب لڑائی ختم کر کے میل ملاپ اور امن قائم کرنا ہے۔

urdu-language-776.q: “عداوت” کے قریب ترین معنی کون سے ہیں؟
urdu-language-776.e: «عداوت» دشمنی اور بغض کو کہتے ہیں، اس لیے دیے گئے اختیارات میں قریب ترین معنی «نفرت» ہے۔

urdu-language-777.q: “حریت” کے قریب ترین معنی کون سے ہیں؟
urdu-language-777.e: «حریت» عربی لفظ «حر» (آزاد) سے ہے اور اس کا مطلب آزادی ہے۔

urdu-language-822.e: «غریب» تنگ دست کو اور «امیر» دولت مند کو کہتے ہیں، اس لیے دونوں ایک دوسرے کے متضاد ہیں۔

urdu-language-823.e: «پرانا» اور «نیا» ایک دوسرے کے متضاد ہیں۔

urdu-language-826.e: «غائب» موجود نہ ہونے اور «حاضر» موجود ہونے کو کہتے ہیں، اس لیے یہ متضاد ہیں۔

urdu-language-827.e: «رد» کسی چیز کو نامنظور کرنے اور «قبول» منظور کرنے کو کہتے ہیں۔

urdu-language-828.e: «مایوسی» ناامیدی کو کہتے ہیں، اس کا متضاد «امید» ہے۔

urdu-language-829.e: «اختلاف» الگ رائے یا جدائی کو اور «اتحاد» یکجہتی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، اس لیے دیے گئے اختیارات میں یہی متضاد ہے۔
